title: Reproducible research experiment report
description: Every experiment produces a consistently structured report whose records are backed by evidence collected outside the process that ran the experiment.

applicability.description: Single-process, CPU-only experiments whose outputs are files in one directory.

requirements.title: Artifact conforms to the IR schema
Every listed output exists and matches its recorded size and SHA-256
Every reported metric equals the value at its pointer in a hashed output
requirements.rationale: A metric in the report must be traceable to a file whose integrity R-002 covers.

requirements.title: Source, environment, dataset, config, execution and output digests are marked as recorded by the collector
requirements.rationale: Producer-asserted metadata is a claim, not evidence. The mark is a field in the artifact; it is only as trustworthy as the place the artifact was written (docs/trust-model.md).

requirements.title: Source is pinned to a clean revision or a hashed snapshot
Every finding references metrics, figures or outputs that exist in the artifact
requirements.rationale: Checks that support is cited, not that the citation justifies the statement (see R-009).

requirements.title: A re-execution reproduces the metrics
requirements.rationale: Metrics are compared exactly in an equal environment. Wall-clock durations never repeat, so a metric whose name ends in _seconds may differ by up to half of the larger value. The tolerance is a placeholder with one benchmark behind it (open question Q5).

requirements.title: Findings and limitations are justified by the evidence
The artifact is a measurement and contains metrics, a report and at least one finding
requirements.rationale: R-002, R-003 and R-007 check every listed item, so an artifact that lists nothing passes them. A fixture must never be accepted as a result.

requirements.title: Names are unique and every figure points at listed outputs
requirements.rationale: A duplicated metric name makes a citation ambiguous; a figure whose files are not hashed outputs is not covered by R-002.
